title: A nurse-led titration clinic for heart failure medicines in a district general hospital: service evaluation plan
abstract: Aim: to raise the proportion of patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction on at least half the target dose of every indicated class from about 29 percent to 60 percent within 6 months of referral. Setting: a district general hospital heart failure service. Intervention: fortnightly nurse-led titration under a signed-off protocol. Measures: doses reached, hyperkalaemia, hypotension and kidney function falls, missed visits by deprivation. Results will be reported after 12 months of operation.
introduction: Randomised and pooled evidence shows that nurse-led titration raises doses and reduces admissions. The local question is whether a new clinic reaches these results safely and equitably, not whether nurse-led titration works.
methods: Registered service evaluation. All referred patients are counted; measures are defined before opening and reported monthly with 95 percent intervals against a six-month baseline from the clinic list.
results: No data have been collected yet. The report will present monthly cohorts, balancing measures and missed visits by deprivation fifth.
discussion: The discussion will compare local results with the retrieved randomised and service reports and state what the service changes next.
limitations: No comparison group; referral selection; primary care results may be missed.
conclusion: To be written after 12 months; it will describe the service and will not claim a causal effect.
summary: Service evaluation report structure with results left empty.
